text:
maura: Kicking off a concurrency sweep for the new v2 quant runner. Quick heads-up: initial run shows p95 latency jump between 4->8 conc and cost/token increases ~30%. Command I ran:
```
./perf-runner --model redwood-v2-qint8 --concurrency 1,2,4,8,16 --seq 1024 --prefetch 0.5 --metric p95
```
Can folks triage before we push to nightly? :eyes:

jon: Saw this in a small QA run earlier, similar pattern. My suspicion is KV cache warmup + a fallback path hitting full decode. p95 climbs when cache hit rate dips under ~70%.

akshay: Confirming cost numbers from the charge logs: cost-per-token jumps where throughput drops. Snapshot from billing log: `tokens=1.9M, cost=0.023`, then later `tokens=1.3M, cost=0.030` for same time window. Not expected for quantized runner.

ci-bot: CI job `perf-eval/v2-quant-concurrency` failed: `reporter: failed to ingest p95 metric (500)`. Full CI output attached to build 2839.

maura: @lin can you check runner config we deployed to perf infra? It might be missing the `enable_prefix_cache` flag that was toggled for qint8-v1. If cache is off we might be decoding full context every request.

lin: digging now. Quick note: the perf infra uses the `runner-config/prod-eval.json` baked by CI. I see "prefix_cache": true in the repo, but the actual instance config has `prefix_cache: false` due to templating bug in the deploy pipeline (we didn't carry the new field into the cloud-init template). Repro: started a local runner with `prefix_cache=false` and recreated the p95 spike.

jon: that matches. Also noticed our dashboard shows token counts lower than the runner logs -> I think CI reporter is sampling token counts from the wrong step (we log tokens per-shard but reporter sums shards incorrectly when concurrency>4). So two separate issues: cache misconfig + reporter sum bug.

akshay: Proposed actions:
- revert perf infra to previous runner image (hotfix) OR flip `prefix_cache=true` on current nodes
- patch CI reporter to use `total_tokens` field instead of per-shard naive sum
- re-run sweep with `--prefetch 0.2` (lower prefetch to avoid extra memory pressure)

maura: I'll patch the deploy template and flip the flag on one pool (canary) first. @sre-bot please add a short incident note for perf regression and link to canary test.

sre-bot: Incident created: PERF-2026-081. Priority: P3. Assigned: eng-ml oncall. Link: https://redwood.incidents/PERF-2026-081

lin: Patch ready for the templating step and a follow-up PR to reporter. Putting a small config diff in the PR: ```diff
- prefix_cache: false
+ prefix_cache: true
+ kv_cache_max_entries: 1024
```

maura: Nice. After flip canary, let's run a short 10-min sweep 1-16 conc and capture p50/p95/cost. If that looks good we'll roll to the rest of perf infra and re-run nightly. Also add an automated check in CI that validates `prefix_cache` present in final deployed config (simple jq assertion).

jon: Agreed. If canary still shows jitter, next step is to instrument KV cache hit rate per-request and gate rollout on >85% hit rate.

akshay: I'll hold off on billing alerts until we confirm the reporter fix. Running repro now locally with `prefix_cache=false` to produce a failing trace I can attach to the PR.

maura: Thanks team. Short action list: maura flips flag on canary, lin lands templating fix, akshay reproduces traces for PR, jon prepares gating metrics. We'll reconvene in ~30m in this thread with results. :thumbsup:
